questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: The work function of a metal depends mainly on:
options: The frequency of the incident light.
The intensity of the incident light.
The nature of the metal and its surface conditions.
The time of exposure to light.
questions.explanation: The work function is a material property determined by the atomic structure and surface characteristics. It is independent of the incident radiation's properties.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of a particle with its momentum (p)?
options: A straight line passing through the origin.
A straight line parallel to the momentum axis.
questions.explanation: λ = h/p implies that λ is inversely proportional to p. The graph of y = k/x is a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: If the frequency of incident light falling on a photosensitive metal is doubled, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons will:
questions.explanation: K_max = hν - Φ. If frequency doubles (2ν), new K' = 2hν - Φ = 2(hν - Φ) + Φ = 2K_max + Φ. Since Φ > 0, K' > 2K_max.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: A proton and an electron have the same kinetic energy. Which of the following statements is true regarding their de Broglie wavelengths?
options: The relationship depends on the magnitude of the velocity.
questions.explanation: λ = h / √(2mK). For constant K, λ ∝ 1/√m. Since m_p > m_e, λ_p < λ_e.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: What is the momentum of a photon of frequency ν?
questions.explanation: Momentum p = E/c. Since E = hν, p = hν/c.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: In a photoelectric effect experiment, if the intensity of the incident light is increased while keeping the frequency constant (above threshold), which of the following increases?
questions.explanation: Intensity relates to the number of photons. More photons release more electrons, increasing the current. Other parameters depend on frequency or material.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: What does the magnitude of the y-intercept (|V_k|) multiplied by the elementary charge (e) represent physically?
questions.explanation: V₀ = (h/e)ν - (Φ/e). The y-intercept is -Φ/e. Its magnitude multiplied by e gives Φ (Work function).
questions.imagePrompt: A graph showing the variation of Stopping Potential (V_0) on the y-axis versus the Frequency of incident radiation (ν) on the x-axis. The straight line intersects the negative y-axis at a point -V_k.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: Passage: Power 3.2 mW, Distance 0.8 m, Sphere radius 8 mm. What is the number of photons striking the metallic sphere per second?
questions.explanation: Fraction of power = Area_sphere / Area_shell = πr² / 4πR² = (1/4)(r/R)². P_inc = P_source × (1/4) × (8e-3 / 0.8)² = 0.8e-7 W. Photon energy E = 5eV = 8e-19 J. N = P_inc/E = 10¹¹.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: What is the saturation photocurrent expected from the sphere?
questions.explanation: Efficiency 10⁻⁶. n_e = 10¹¹ × 10⁻⁶ = 10⁵ e/s. I = n_e × e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁴ A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: After a long time, the sphere becomes charged due to the loss of electrons. What is the maximum potential acquired by the sphere relative to infinity (stopping the emission)?
questions.explanation: Emission stops when potential V = Stopping Potential V₀. eV₀ = E - Φ = 5 - 3 = 2 eV. So V = 2.0 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: Light of wavelength λ gives stopping potential V₁. Wavelength 3λ gives V₂. If V₁ = 4V₂, what is the threshold wavelength λ₀?
questions.explanation: Solve the system: V ∝ (1/λ - 1/λ₀). (1/λ - 1/λ₀) = 4(1/3λ - 1/λ₀). Solving gives λ₀ = 9λ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: A parallel beam of light of intensity I is incident at an angle θ (with the normal) on a perfectly plane reflecting surface of area A. The force exerted by the light on the surface is:
questions.explanation: Power incident P = IA cosθ. Momentum incident normal to surface = (P/c) cosθ = (IA cos²θ)/c. For reflection, change is double. Force = 2IA cos²θ / c.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: An electron in H-atom jumps n=4 to n=1. Photon ejects electron from metal (Φ=2.75 eV). B-field = 2e-4 T. Radius of electron path?
questions.explanation: Photon E = 13.6(1 - 1/16) = 12.75 eV. KE_max = 12.75 - 2.75 = 10 eV. Radius R = √(2mK)/eB. Calculating gives approx 5.3 cm, closest option 5.0 cm.
questions.imagePrompt: A diagram shows a hydrogen atom in an excited state emitting a photon. This photon strikes a metal plate in a vacuum photocell. The photoelectrons emitted enter a region with a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to their velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: If kinetic energy increases by ΔK (small), the fractional change in de Broglie wavelength is approximately:
questions.explanation: λ = h/√(2mK) ∝ K^(-1/2). Log diff: Δλ/λ = -1/2 (ΔK/K).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: Particle in 1D box length L, ground state speed v₁. Box compressed to L/3, speed in n=2 state v₂. v₂/v₁ is:
questions.explanation: v = nh / (2mL). v₁ = h/2mL. v₂ = 2h / (2m(L/3)) = 6h/2mL = 6v₁.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: Absorbing sphere radius r density ρ at distance D from power P. Initial acceleration a?
questions.explanation: Force F = (P/4πD²)(πr²)/c. Mass m = 4/3 πr³ρ. a = F/m = [P r² / 4cD²] / [4/3 πr³ ρ] = 3P / (16πρrcD²).
